query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.target_system: Multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) system, specifically a refractory-based composition (e.g., Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V or Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr) currently in a cast form with limited ductility, targeted for nanocrystalline grain refinement (<50 nm) and dual-phase solid solution stabilization.

evidence_appraisal.record_system: Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory HEA with Cr addition
evidence_appraisal.difference_from_target: Target requires nanocrystalline (<50 nm) dual-phase solid solution; this record shows Cr addition forming a brittle Laves intermetallic phase (though reticulated) and achieving high strength, but not explicitly nanocrystalline grain sizes or avoiding intermetallics entirely.
evidence_appraisal.reason: Transfers the concept of strength enhancement via secondary phase formation and solid solution hardening in refractory MPEAs. However, it contradicts the target constraint of avoiding brittle intermetallics (Laves phase) and does not demonstrate the specific nanocrystalline grain refinement mechanism required.

evidence_appraisal.record_system: Cr-Mo-Nb-W-V refractory HEA processed by Mechanical Alloying (MA) and Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS)
evidence_appraisal.difference_from_target: Target seeks <50 nm grains and dual-phase solid solution; this record achieves BCC solid solution via MA/SPS but reports grain coarsening at higher sintering temperatures (1400°C) and partial decomposition to Laves phases/oxides.
evidence_appraisal.reason: Directly demonstrates that Mechanical Alloying followed by SPS can produce nanocrystalline BCC solid solutions in refractory MPEAs. The mechanism of severe plastic deformation (MA) followed by low-temperature consolidation (SPS) is the exact route needed to achieve <50 nm grains while suppressing intermetallic formation if temperature is controlled.

Useful for defining the stability boundary of the dual-phase structure.

generation.hypothesis: To achieve a nanocrystalline (<50 nm) dual-phase solid solution structure in a brittle cast refractory MPEA (e.g., Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V) without forming brittle intermetallics, the alloy must be processed via Mechanical Alloying (MA) to induce severe plastic deformation and amorphization, followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at a strictly controlled low temperature (e.g., 900–1000 °C) to consolidate the powder while suppressing grain growth and intermetallic precipitation. The phase constitution should be tuned to a dual-phase BCC (disordered) + BCC (ordered) or BCC + FCC solid solution (if VEC allows) by adjusting the Valence Electron Concentration (VEC) to be between 4.4 and 6.0 and maintaining atomic size difference (δ) < 6.6% to ensure thermodynamic stability of the solid solution phases. This route leverages the high defect density from MA to drive grain refinement and the rapid heating/cooling of SPS to kinetically trap the nanocrystalline state.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast refractory multi-principal element alloy (e.g., Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V) with coarse grains (>10 µm), limited ductility, and potential for brittle intermetallic formation upon cooling.
generation.intervention: Mechanical Alloying (MA) of elemental powders for 40+ hours to achieve nanocrystalline/amorphous state, followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 900–1000 °C under vacuum/inert atmosphere for 10–30 minutes.
generation.conditions: MA: 300–500 rpm, ball-to-powder ratio 10:1, inert gas. SPS: 900–1000 °C, 50–100 MPa pressure, heating rate >100 °C/min, hold time <30 min.
generation.structural_mediator: Severe plastic deformation induced grain boundaries and high dislocation density from MA; rapid thermal consolidation from SPS preventing grain coarsening and intermetallic nucleation.
generation.mechanism: Derived from PMC7866258 and PMC5978046: Mechanical Alloying introduces high energy defects and reduces grain size to the nanometer scale via repeated cold welding and fracturing. SPS provides rapid densification at temperatures below the threshold for significant grain growth or intermetallic precipitation (unlike PMC7866258 where 1400°C caused coarsening). The phase constitution is stabilized by thermodynamic criteria from PMC7513042 (VEC < 6.87, δ < 6.6%) to ensure a dual-phase solid solution (e.g., disordered BCC + ordered BCC or BCC + FCC) rather than brittle intermetallics (like Laves phases seen in PMC10759803).
generation.predicted_outcome: A bulk alloy with average grain size < 50 nm, yield strength > 2000 MPa (due to Hall-Petch and solid solution strengthening), hardness > 600 Hv, and ductility > 10% (due to dual-phase solid solution preventing brittle fracture), with no detectable brittle intermetallic phases (e.g., Laves, TiO) by XRD.
generation.baseline: Cast refractory MPEA with coarse grains, yield strength ~1000–1200 MPa, and ductility < 5% due to brittle intermetallics or coarse grain boundaries.
generation.boundary: The nanocrystalline dual-phase structure becomes unstable if SPS temperature exceeds 1100 °C (leading to grain coarsening and potential Laves phase formation as seen in PMC7866258) or if VEC exceeds 6.87 (promoting brittle BCC or intermetallics as per PMC7513042).
generation.uncertainty: High uncertainty regarding the exact VEC threshold for a specific refractory system to form a *dual-phase* solid solution without any intermetallics; the stability of the ordered BCC phase at room temperature in refractory systems is less documented than in Al-containing systems (PMC6197204).

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare the target refractory MPEA via MA/SPS at 950 °C. Perform a control experiment varying the SPS temperature to 1200 °C. Analyze both samples using X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM).
measurements: Presence of Laves or other intermetallic phases (TEM/EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 950 °C sample shows grain size > 50 nm or the presence of brittle intermetallic phases (e.g., Laves), the hypothesis is falsified. If the 1200 °C sample shows significantly higher ductility or no intermetallics, the hypothesis regarding the temperature boundary is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract Concurrent strength–ductility improvement of HfMoTaTiZr is achieved via Cr addition and the underlying strengthening mechanism was discussed. 4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase. The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 is 535.8 Hv 0.3 , 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr. The yield strength and fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr. Solid solution hardening and the presence of the intermetallic Laves phase are believed to be responsible for the enhancement in strength and the formation of a reticulated structure of the Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 results in the improvement in ductility.

Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties

In this study, bulk samples of a CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (HEA) were obtained for the first time by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed (MA) powders at 1200 °C, 1300 °C, and 1400 °C. Microstructure evolution, phase formation as well as wear and corrosion behavior were investigated. The MA powders’ phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution. The solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases under the sintering, such as Cr 2 Nb and (Fe, Cr)Nb, and NbVO 4 -VO oxides mixture. The temperature increase to 1400 °C led to a grain coarsening of the BCC phase and decreased the Laves phase content accompanied by precipitation at the grain boundaries. The sintered samples showed high hardness and compressive strength (2700–2800 MPa) at room temperature. The wear tests demonstrated excellent results in comparison to conventional wear-resistant composites. The obtained samples also exhibited high corrosion resistance under electrochemical tests in H 2 SO 4 solution.
